## Scope

The six linked tables contain patients, samples, interpreted variants, reports,
clinical measurements and survival outcomes. Readers retain source observations;
the database does not infer patient identity, annotation, pathogenicity or assay
coverage from absent fields. Raw FASTQ reads and BAM alignments remain inspectable
reader results and cannot be added as interpreted variants.

## A runnable import

This example uses only synthetic records and creates its own temporary files.
Identifiers are supplied explicitly, including the link from each sample to a
patient.

```{r import}
library(molpathR)
source_dir <- tempfile("molpath-example-")
dir.create(source_dir)
pathology <- file.path(source_dir, "pathology.csv")
clinical <- file.path(source_dir, "clinical.csv")
survival_file <- file.path(source_dir, "survival.csv")
writeLines(c(
  "patient_id,name,sex,sample_id,sample_type,diagnosis,report_date",
  "P1,Synthetic One,F,S1,FFPE,Example A,2025-01-01",
  "P2,Synthetic Two,M,S2,FFPE,Example B,2025-01-02"
), pathology)
writeLines(c(
  "patient_id;parameter;value;unit;date;source",
  "P1;marker;17;U;2025-01-01;synthetic",
  "P2;marker;23;U;2025-01-02;synthetic"
), clinical)
writeLines(c(
  "patient_id,os_months,os_status,pfs_months,pfs_status",
  "P1,12,0,8,0",
  "P2,18,1,10,1"
), survival_file)
db <- mp_build_db(
  mp_read_nexus_pathology(pathology),
  mp_read_nexus_clinical(clinical),
  mp_read_survival(survival_file)
)
mp_validate_db(db)$valid
mp_get_patient(db, "P1")$clinical
```

CSV, semicolon-delimited and tab-delimited exports are detected by their actual
fields. Field aliases match whole column names, ignoring case and surrounding
header whitespace. `patient_id_backup` is preserved as an extra source column;
it does not replace `patient_id`. Multiple recognized aliases for one field are
ambiguous and require reconciliation. Survival event values must be exactly 0
(censored), 1 (event), or missing; fractional values are never truncated. Observed
times must be finite and nonnegative. Dates use ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` values.

## VCF calls and missing annotations

The reader preserves ID, INFO, FORMAT and each sample's raw token regardless of
optional typed-reader installations. Original header lines and declared sample
names are in `parsed$metadata`. Database integration expands observed
non-reference GT alleles, while retaining source genomic fields and genotype
information. Each normalized row keeps its original sample token in
`sample_fields`, interpreted by `format`; raw sample names cannot overwrite gene
annotations or model identifiers. It does not derive gene effects or pathogenicity from coordinates.

```{r vcf}
vcf <- file.path(source_dir, "calls.vcf")
writeLines(c(
  "##fileformat=VCFv4.2",
  "#CHROM\tPOS\tID\tREF\tALT\tQUAL\tFILTER\tINFO\tFORMAT\tS1\tS2",
  "1\t100\t.\tA\tG\t50\tPASS\tDP=50\tGT:DP\t0/1:20\t0/0:30"
), vcf)
parsed <- mp_read_vcf(vcf)
parsed$data
linked <- mp_add_data(db, parsed)
linked$variants[, c("sample_id", "variant", "genotype", "gene", "classification")]
mp_validate_db(linked)$valid
```

A site-only VCF or sample measurements without GT do not establish a usable
sample call. Inspect the parsed table, then supply an explicitly normalized
`sample_id`/`variant` table after independent calling/annotation if that is the
intended input. Reference or uncalled genotypes are not evidence of a wild-type
gene: the package has no assay-coverage model.

## Reports and raw sequencing

| Reader | Stored observations and boundary |
|---|---|
| `mp_read_xml_report()` | Explicit XML patient/sample IDs and variant text; namespace-aware generic template |
| `mp_read_pdf_report()` | Extracted text sections; no OCR or inferred patient/sample identity |
| `mp_read_fastq()` | Raw read IDs, sequences and qualities; `n` selects the first records, not a random sample |
| `mp_read_bam()` | Explicit alignment fields, optionally restricted to one genomic region |
| `mp_read_auto()` | Recognized source schema; unrecognized or ambiguous tabular layouts raise an error |

The generic report templates are not vendor-certified. XML without a known link
and PDF text can remain incomplete report evidence; inspect it before assigning
an identity. The complete extracted PDF pages and text are retained in parser metadata; report
summaries use the full text even when heuristic sections omit a heading.
Image-only PDF reports require an external, verified transcription
or OCR process. FASTQ/BAM database integration is refused because alignment and
variant interpretation are separate tasks. The raw reader results remain usable.

For an extensionless uploaded file, pass its original filename using
`mp_read_auto(path, source_name = "clinical.csv")`. Dispatch uses a disposable
copy with that filename and records its basename, not a deleted upload path.

## Validation, merging and persistence

Constructed databases always contain the six typed tables. Missing patient/sample
links remain explicit and make `mp_validate_db(db)$valid` false, even when the
parent table is empty. Malformed schemas, nonfinite measures, invalid event codes
and duplicate primary IDs raise an error. Merge identical records or complementary
missing attributes; resolve conflicting observed attributes deliberately.

```{r persistence}
saved <- file.path(source_dir, "database.rds")
mp_save_db(linked, saved)
restored <- mp_load_db(saved)
identical(restored, linked)
unlink(source_dir, recursive = TRUE)
```

Saving stages and verifies the complete RDS before replacement. A failed
replacement restores the previous destination or reports the preserved recovery
path. Use one writer per destination. Incomplete links are reported on save and
remain inspectable after reload; they are not silently repaired.

Older zero-column empty tables and one-row metadata tibbles are normalized on
load. ISO date strings are normalized to `Date`. Malformed nonempty tables or
conflicting identities require explicit repair; keep the original RDS and review
the reported field rather than fabricating missing clinical information.
